liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Morning Dew** (3 reviews): Reviewer says the performance soars and is the reason to sit through the poor recording; The exit starts near 7:55 in pin-drop quiet; Garcia sounds fast and fluent as it builds [9][14][18]
- **Loser** (1 review): Reviewer singles out the lead in Loser as amazing [19]
- **Deal** (1 review): Reviewer calls Jerry's lead in Deal brilliant [19]
- **Althea** (1 review): Reviewer calls the jam at the end of Althea all-time [15]

## The recordings

- **gd80-08-20.naks.munder.8740.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 21 songs; 159 min; rated 2.88/5 by 17 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the audience recording very poor, though not the worst they have heard; Reviewer finds the sound good compared with other recordings on the site; Reviewer finds the audience recording lousy and says it detracts from the show [9][11][13][14][16][18]
- **gd1980-08-20.151836.aud.unknown.andrewf.t-flac16**: audience recording; 21 songs; 149 min [2]
- **gd1980-08-20.147370.s1.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 10 songs; 71 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [4]
- **gd1980-08-20.147366.s1.sbd.miller.flac24**: soundboard; 10 songs; 71 min [6]

## Around the show

- Reviewer found the neighborhood rough, with acid openly sold on the street outside [8]
- The balcony swayed noticeably, and the reviewer spent much of the show watching dancers in a trance [8]
- The crowd sounds rowdy, with many clap-alongs early in the show [13]
- The audience can be heard going wild during Morning Dew [16]
- Reviewer hitchhiked from Philly to Chicago via Indianapolis in 95 degree heat to see a friend, then attended the show [17]
- The theater was small and intimate; reviewer walked right up the aisle to the front with no hassle [18]
- Reviewer says Morning Dew was played only once in 1978 and once in 1979, so 1980 versions are welcome [14]
- Reviewer notes this Morning Dew was one of only four played in 1980 [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd80-08-20.naks.munder.8740.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: Nak 700's w/shotgun caps [1]. Also: Reviewer's early-80s tape of this show was probably a couple of generations down from this source; Recorded from the balcony with Nakamichi 700s and shotgun capsules into a Sony TC-158 cassette deck, then DAT, then CD; Transfer came via Mark Lindenbaum and was seeded to etree by Willy [1][19]
- **gd1980-08-20.151836.aud.unknown.andrewf.t-flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Andrew F.; source: AUD of unknown lineage > ? > lo-gen cassette via Richie & Rip. [2]. Also: Beat It On Down The Line had a mic or cable problem; left channel was pasted over right; Parts of Althea and U.S. Blues were patched, and Jack Straw, Loser and Drums were patched from the ID-8740 source [2]
- **gd1980-08-20.147370.s1.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > Cassette Master (Maxell UDXL-II) [4]. Also: Chain is Nakamichi 700 shotguns to cassette master to DAT to CD, shnid 8740; Looks Like Rain from 6:05 to 6:39 is supplied by the 8740 source [4]
- **gd1980-08-20.147366.s1.sbd.miller.flac24**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > Cassette Master (Maxell UDXL-II) [6]. Also: Chain is Nakamichi 700 shotguns to cassette master to DAT to CD, shnid 8740 [6]
